narrative.overview:
The app is visited in seconds, mid-game: alt-tab in, read the state at a glance, mark something or find the
next collectible, and back to the game. Every visual decision serves that stop: dark, calm surfaces that don't
glare after a dark game, state you can read without hunting (the big found count, the progress bar, collected
pins greyed out with a green check), keyboard hints right on the controls (`/`, `N`, `C`), and one color for
"act here", with nothing in the chrome competing with the map.

The interface is a quiet set of dark slate layers. The color on screen belongs to the game: its map tiles,
marker icons and cover art. The app adds just three signals: **Pit-Lane Cyan** for the one thing to do or the
thing in focus, **Green Flag** for done, and gold ★ for what counts toward progress. Surfaces have two heights:
cards sit on the page with a faint shadow and a hairline of top light, and only things that float above it
(popups, menus, the toast, the update banner) cast a real shadow. The map sidebar is dense and compact (328px,
12–16px insets) because it sits beside the map. The Library is airier: a centred 1,120px column, headed
sections, cover-topped game cards and a blurred sticky top bar.

Controls are **soft and friendly**: gently rounded corners (8px), pill-shaped chips, one drawn icon set with
round strokes, and state changes that ease in over about 150ms (and switch off under reduced motion). Two looks
are explicitly rejected: **a busy map website** (ads, banners, upsells, clutter around the map) and **a light,
bright app** (white surfaces that glare when you alt-tab from a dark game).
keyCharacteristics: Dark everywhere: page, panels, popups, menus, tooltips, map controls, select menus and scrollbars.
One accent (Pit-Lane Cyan) for action and focus; green means done and nothing else.
The game's art carries the color; the app's chrome stays neutral slate.
Readable at a glance: a 24px found count, tabular numbers, greyed collected pins, key hints on controls.
Soft, compact controls: 8px corners, pill chips, 34px standard height, one round-stroke icon set.
Two heights: resting surfaces with a faint lift, floating ones with a real shadow.

rules.name: The Pit-Lane Rule
rules.body: Pit-Lane Cyan marks the action or the focus: one primary button per area, the field you're typing in, the filter that's on. It never fills a panel or a large area.

rules.name: The Green Flag Rule
rules.body: Green means done, and only done: collected, finished, complete. Never use it for a generic "success" message or a call to action.

rules.name: The Game Owns the Color Rule
rules.body: The app's chrome stays in slate neutrals so the game's map, icons and covers are the most colorful things on screen. New color goes into the game's content, not the interface.

rules.name: The System Voice Rule
rules.body: One family, the OS's own UI font. Add hierarchy with weight (650 or 700) and size steps of a pixel or two; never with a display face. Monospace is for keys, paths and code, not decoration.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number someone compares at a glance (counts, percentages, progress, sizes, the download log, the version) uses tabular numerals so columns don't jitter as values change.

rules.name: The Two Heights Rule
rules.body: A surface either rests (tone, hairline, Rest shadow and top light) or floats (Float shadow). There is no third, in-between elevation, and nothing at rest gets Float.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing interactive has square corners: 8px on controls, 6px on small ones, 12px on containers, a pill for anything that toggles or tags. The only square edges are full-width list rows in the sidebar.

dos: **Do** keep every surface dark: Night Asphalt (#0b0f14) for the page, Slate Panel (#151b23) for panels and popups, and Raised Slate (#1b222c) for controls and menus, including Leaflet's zoom bar, tooltips, select option menus and scrollbars.
**Do** use Pit-Lane Cyan (#5ec8ff) for one primary action per area and for every focus state (a 2px outline with a 2px offset; fields get the 3px focus ring).
**Do** show "collected" with Green Flag (#3ddc84) and a drawn check, and dim collected pins (grayscale, 55% opacity) instead of hiding them.
**Do** use tabular numerals for counts, percentages, progress, sizes and the version.
**Do** keep controls soft and friendly: 8px corners on buttons and fields, pills for chips, 150ms transitions on the shared ease.
**Do** draw every icon from the one round-stroke set through masks, and put key hints on the controls they trigger.
**Do** keep controls compact beside the map: 34px standard, 28px small, 26px chips, a 328px sidebar.
donts: **Don't** add light themes, white panels or bright surfaces. The app must never feel like "a light, bright app" that glares after a dark game.
**Don't** surround the map with banners, promos, badges or decoration. It must never feel like "a busy map website"; the update banner appears only when there is an update and can be dismissed.
**Don't** use a map site's colors, logo or look anywhere in the app.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue or a display typeface.
**Don't** use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons.
**Don't** give a resting surface the Float shadow; Float is for floating things.
**Don't** use Green Flag for anything but done, or Danger Coral for anything but destructive actions and errors.
